n: David challenges the rulers and judges: do you really judge fairly? The word translated “congregation” may instead mean “mighty ones” or “gods” — people in power who should protect justice.

f.g: The Hebrew is uncertain; many read “O gods” or “mighty ones” — rulers acting as judges.

n: No — in their hearts they plan evil and hand out violence instead of justice, as if weighing it on scales.

f.w: ye weigh the violence of your hands
f.g: Instead of weighing justice on the scales, they deal out violence.

n: The wicked have gone wrong for as long as anyone can remember, lying from their earliest days. This is poetic exaggeration for deep-rooted corruption.

f.g: A poetic way of saying they have strayed for a long time; scripture also teaches children are born innocent.

n: Their words are poison like a snake’s — like a cobra that refuses to hear.

f.g: A venomous snake, probably a cobra.

n: Snake charmers can’t control them, no matter how skilled. These leaders refuse every appeal to conscience.

f.g: Snake charmers, who used music or chants to control snakes.

n: David asks God to disarm these predators — break the teeth of these young lions so they can’t devour the weak.
May they drain away like water that runs into the ground; may their arrows fall broken.

f.g: Like headless arrows — blunted and useless.

n: May they vanish like a snail leaving a dissolving trail, or like a stillborn child who never sees daylight. These are vivid images of complete futility.

f.g: Ancient people thought snails melted away as they moved, leaving slime.

n: Faster than a cooking pot can heat over burning thorns, God will sweep them away like a storm. Judgment will come swiftly.

f.w: Before your pots can feel the thorns
f.g: Thorn bushes were quick fuel for cooking fires; this means very suddenly.

n: The righteous will rejoice when justice comes. The bloody image is battlefield language from the ancient world, expressing total victory of good over evil, not personal cruelty.

f.w: wash his feet in the blood of the wicked
f.g: Ancient war imagery for complete victory.

n: Then people will say: there really is a reward for the righteous, and there really is a God who judges on earth. Justice vindicates faith.

f.w: there is a reward for the righteous
